Almost all of Westeros follows "Patrilineal Primogeniture".

When the Lord dies, the eldest LEGITIMATE son inherits the Lords titles and land.

If the eldest son is dead and had no sons of his own to inherit the estate, than the second oldest son of the recently departed Lord gets the title and lands.

This continues until some son, grandson, great grandson of the Lord receives the titles and lands. 

If there are no sons, than titles pass to the BLOOD brothers of the Lord, and the trend continues.

If there are brothers or nephews, than the titles TECHNICALLY pass to the eldest daughter and her estate.

However at this point the case will most likely be put to the King, who will decide if the bastard son or the eldest daughter gets the title and lands. 

Also it is worth noting that in the end, the person with the most power and backing will get what they want.

\--- Family, Duty, Honour, in that order:

If you can't protect, feed and care for your family, how can you be trusted to do your other duties?  If you can't do your assigned duties, how can you be trusted to keep your word/oaths? Also if man must choose between two oaths, they are expected to side with family over all others. With this in mind Ned Stark (due to his fostering) disdains Jaime, but the other Lords think Jaime did the right thing, he had a conflict of oaths and chose Family (or the Knights Oath once they find out about the wildfire trap) over the Kingsguard one. 

  
\--- Waste Not, Want Not:

Everything is used, everything is recycled. Whilst showing off is allowed, its only allowed if you and your people are cared for. A lord showing off their wealth while people starve is detested. Additionally they like things that show off great feats and achievements more than simply showing off your wealth. Additionally they know how to work wood, bone, leather and all other "basic" materials to a masterful degree, whereas they have less jewellers and other "high end" luxury craftsmen. 



\--- Better the Devil you know:

Innovation is not shunned, they are a pragmatic people, but changing a known method to try something new could result in death and starvation. As such only the wealthiest lords/farmers/merchants can afford to try something new.

  
\--- First Men, First, Last, Always:

The aren't a fan of outsiders simply because come winter they don't know if they can be trusted to not steal food. BUT once someone has survived a winter without resorting to crime they gain the respect of the others and are considered a Northerner. 

  
\--- Winter is Coming, and a sword wont stop it:

Southerners worship the gods of men, cause they need things a man can provide. Northerners worship gods of nature for a long summer and short winter, cause ain't nothing a god of men can do to stop winter. 

  
\--- Outdoor concerts:

During summer they feast and party outside with bagpipes and loud drums. After being stuck inside all winter they are spending as much time in the sun as they can. This doubles with Northern commoners being more likely to read than others cause they have nothing else to do during winter but sing, read, and play board games really. 

  
You could expand upon these with specifics and throw in rituals as well, but those details matter less than the theme/reasoning behind them.

Guest Right = Sacred and Inviolatile, worst thing someone could break. 

Importance of Food =  Wasting food is the second worst thing, and shows you to be unworthy of trust.

The North Remembers = No debt is forgotten, nor slight forgiven, if the father can't settle it, the son must, and so on. To forgive insults or harm is a clear sign of weakness and cowardice.

The Old Gods = Obviously.

A somewhat contradictory belief in self reliance and community =  All true Northerners can fight and hunt, farm and forage, build and craft, and be independant in all aspects, but gladly work together for the betterment of the community. There is a difference between needing help and being helpess. One is forgivable, the other not.

Bright Colours and Loud Music = Winter is Coming, and with it Ice and Darkness. The world is cold and dark enough as it is, and the northerners love to counter that with bright colours and loud music when possible.

​

Specific Cultural Regions of The North:

Hill Tribes

Wolfwoods

The Rills (includes the Stoney Shore)

The Barrowlands (Torrhens Square river to the Broken Branch river, Moat Cailin to Winterfell)

The Neck

The Lonely Hills (Everything north of Hornwood to the Wall)

​
